findings.issue: Attempted two edits against typos it hallucinated in files it had just written; both edit calls failed and verification showed the files were already correct
findings.suggestion: Before 'fixing' remembered defects in just-written files, grep the file first — the write result already showed the content

findings.issue: Playwright screenshot script placed in /tmp could not resolve the repo-root-installed `playwright` package, costing a turn
findings.suggestion: Run scripts that import project devDependencies from within the project directory

findings.issue: `pkill -f "vite dev"` matched its own bash wrapper and killed the shell (exit 143)
findings.suggestion: Kill by PID or use a pattern that can't match the pkill command itself (e.g. `pkill -f node_modules/.bin/vite`)

findings.issue: No typecheck was ever run despite a `strict: true` tsconfig and ~18 TS/TSX files; correctness was confirmed only via vite build (which transpiles without typechecking) and the runtime tests
findings.suggestion: Add a `typecheck` script and run it once before declaring done

findings.issue: Guessed `tests/helpers.mjs` before listing the tests directory (ENOENT read failure)
findings.suggestion: Minor; list the directory before reading inferred paths

summary: A model session: 70 turns, ~19 minutes, zero fix cycles, first full test run green. It front-loaded spec, tests, data forensics and current-framework verification, wrote the app in one pass, then went beyond the acceptance tests with curl probes and desktop/mobile screenshot comparison against the references, re-running the full suite after its final edit. The only blemishes are self-created trivial waste (hallucinated edits, a /tmp import miss, a self-killing pkill) and a skipped typecheck.
